messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to set priorities for the upcoming 2-week micro-release. Do we land more bugfixes or tuck in the small UX polish requests from Support?

sam: leaning towards bugs for the first cut. customers hitting crashes > minor UX.

jorge: Agreed on crashes, but we should reserve one engineer for high-impact UX (search autocomplete). That one reduces support tickets a lot.

alex: can we quantify? how many user-facing crashes are P0/P1 vs how many UX asks have measurable impact?

lina: Support deck showed 8 unique crash reports since launch (3 repeaters). UX asks ~12 small items but low severity.

maya: ok — proposal: 60% of dev capacity to P0/P1 bug queue, 20% to regression/backstop for other infra, 20% to 1-2 high-ROI UX items. Thoughts?

sam: that split sounds good. also request we block a day for the perf team to look at a tokenization regression, it's spiking cost.

jorge: we should add a gating rule: any bug that has >3 incoming tickets gets automatic priority bump. That prevents triage lag.

alex: +1. Also propose we create a small telemetry check for the UX change so we can measure impact (CTR on suggestions).

lina: can Product Ops own the telemetry check? I can add a quick dashboard and success criteria: +10% suggestions CTR or reduce support threads by 30%.

maya: love it. Okay finalizing: execute 60/20/20 cap split, auto-bump rule for >3 tickets, one UX item (autocomplete) with telemetry. Lina to own dashboard.

product-bot: Reminder: please add rollout plan to the release doc and tag stakeholders. Release doc: https://redwood.internal/releases/micro-2 -> @eng @support

sam: noted — adding rollout steps and canary thresholds. propose canary at 5% traffic for 12 hours, watch errors & latency.

jorge: add fallback policy: if errors > 0.5% revert automatically.

alex: how do we communicate scope to customers who asked for the bigger UX wishlist?

maya: short answer: ship the high-ROI bits in this wave, publish roadmap for next quarter with the full wishlist and invite beta users. We'll message via release notes + customer success follow-ups.

lina: I'll draft the release note and a paragraph for CSMs.

maya: thx team. I'll put the prioritization and ticket assignments in the sprint board by EOD.

sam: thanks — ping if you need help breaking down tasks. :thumbsup:

alex: +1, thanks.

maya: resolving — follow-ups in #product when sprint board updated.
